name: Spaghetti Carbonara with Guanciale and Pecorino
description: A Roman-inspired pasta made with crisp guanciale, egg yolks, Pecorino, and starchy pasta water. The sauce is finished away from direct heat so it stays smooth and creamy.
abstract: A fast pasta dish for two, made with a small number of bold ingredients.
accessibilitySummary: The instructions are divided into named, numbered steps; quantities and times are included in the text.
recipeIngredient: 75 g guanciale, cut into small cubes
20 g salt for the pasta water

itemListElement.name: Start the pasta water
itemListElement.text: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot and salt it well. Cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente; before draining, reserve about 250 ml of pasta water.

itemListElement.name: Render the guanciale
itemListElement.text: While the pasta cooks, place the guanciale in a cold frying pan and render it slowly over medium heat. Once the cubes are golden and crisp, take the pan off the heat.

itemListElement.name: Make the egg and cheese paste
itemListElement.text: Mix the egg yolks, Pecorino, and plenty of black pepper in a bowl to make a thick paste. Work in two tablespoons of warm pasta water to loosen it slightly.

itemListElement.name: Emulsify the pasta
itemListElement.text: Transfer the still-dripping spaghetti to the pan with the guanciale and toss it thoroughly in the rendered fat. Let the pan cool for two minutes. Add the egg and cheese paste, then keep the pasta and sauce moving. Add pasta water a little at a time until a glossy sauce lightly coats the strands.

itemListElement.name: Serve immediately
itemListElement.text: Divide the carbonara between warmed plates and finish with more Pecorino and black pepper. Serve at once, as the sauce thickens quickly when left to stand.
